Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- Failing test setup:
  - Creates an option -x/--extralongarg with description "This description is Long."
  - Calls HelpFormatter.printHelp(PrintWriter, 22, cmd, "Header", options, 0, 5, "Footer").
  - With width=22, leftPad=0, descPad=5, and a long option label (“-x,--extralongarg”), the description start column (next line tab stop) becomes very large (leftPad + option label width + descPad), likely >= 22.

- Call flow:
  - printHelp(PrintWriter,int,String,String,Options,int,int,String) delegates to printHelp(..., boolean) (lines 466–495).
  - It then calls printOptions(pw, width, options, leftPad, descPad) (line 489), which renders the options text and wraps it. The wrapping of multi-line text ultimately goes through:
    - printWrapped(PrintWriter,int,int,String) (lines 690–696) → renderWrappedText(StringBuffer,int,int,String) (lines 809–852).

- Where the problem occurs:
  - renderWrappedText first computes an initial wrap position via findWrapPos(text, width, 0) (line 812).
  - If wrapping is needed, it appends the first line, and before wrapping subsequent lines it checks:
    - if (nextLineTabStop >= width) throw new IllegalStateException("Total width is less than the width of the argument and indent - no room for the description") (lines 822–827).
  - This check is triggered in the failing test because the indent for continuation lines (nextLineTabStop) is at least as wide as the total width (caused by the long option label plus the descPad). As a result, printHelp throws instead of completing.

- Relation to the reported bug (“infinite loop in the wrapping code”):
  - The infinite loop happens when there is no room left for content on wrapped lines. In previous behavior, the loop in renderWrappedText would repeatedly try to wrap within the indentation:
    - The loop body constructs each subsequent line as text = padding + text.substring(pos).trim(); then re-runs findWrapPos (lines 833–851).
    - When width is less than or equal to the indentation size, findWrapPos keeps returning a position within the padding, so the loop cannot make real progress and may spin.
  - The code contains two safeguards:
    - The explicit guard that throws when nextLineTabStop >= width (lines 822–827) to prevent an infinite loop in this “no room for description” case.
    - A secondary tweak that forces progress if the wrap position falls exactly at nextLineTabStop - 1 (lines 845–848).
  - The test BugCLI162Test.testLongLineChunkingIndentIgnored suggests the desired behavior is to “ignore” the indent when it would overrun the available width (i.e., do not hang and do not throw), letting wrapping proceed with reduced or zero indentation. However, the current implementation throws an exception instead of relaxing or ignoring the indent, causing the test to fail.

- Summary of root cause:
  - With a narrow width (22) and a long option label, the calculated continuation indent (nextLineTabStop) equals or exceeds the total width. renderWrappedText detects this and throws, rather than adapting the indent to allow wrapping. This behavior both explains the historical infinite loop (without such a guard) and the current test failure that expects indent to be ignored instead of raising an exception.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
